end_markets.body:
- International trade / cross-border commodities and minerals
- Domestic real estate (commercial and residential spaces)

demand_drivers.title: Mdna (RHP)
demand_drivers.body:
- Real Estate is likely to remain an important contributor to India's economic expansion, with continued urbanization, rising household incomes, infrastructure development and demand for warehouses, logistics parks, data centers, offices, retail, industrial parks and residential houses expected to support the sector, which is beneficial for the company's Real Estate business.
- International trade dynamics remain subject to evolving bilateral and multilateral trade agreements between India and key trading partners, which continue to exert substantial influence on aggregate demand and cross-border supply chains relevant to the trading division.
- The outlook for urban demand continues to remain mixed and the consumption scenario is expected to increase due to lower personal tax burden.
- The company expects sustained business growth across its Trading and Real Estate divisions, supported by government policy initiatives and strategic focus, though performance will depend on the growth scenario, geopolitical situation, trade protectionism/tariffs and domestic demand conditions.

capex_expansion.title: Expansion (RHP)
capex_expansion.body: The company continues to explore entering the manufacturing sector as a further diversification of its Real Estate and International Trade businesses, though no specific project, site or timeline is disclosed. Company's stake in commercial and residential real estate spaces, held along with its associates, is described as relatively stabilized.

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- Persistent tensions in West Asia, geopolitical resolutions, extended supply chain disruptions and elevated global energy prices exert continuous pressure on global inflation and could affect performance in coming quarters.
- International trade dynamics remain subject to evolving bilateral and multilateral trade agreements between India and key trading partners; trade protectionism, tariffs and trade agreements will influence the company's Trading division.
- As the Company actively engages in international trade operations, it is inherently exposed to currency volatility, managed via an in-house Treasury Management desk and Board-approved Hedging Policy using derivative instruments.
- The rising probability of below normal rainfall and likelihood of El Nino conditions during the monsoon season pose a key risk for the food inflation outlook, affecting the broader domestic demand environment the company depends on.
- India's economy and the company's performance in coming quarters will be affected by the global growth scenario, evolving trade dynamics and sustained elevation in energy prices.
- The company's operations are concentrated in Real Estate and International Trade, both explicitly flagged as sensitive to urban demand conditions, infrastructure investment cycles and cross-border trade corridors.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Management has been constantly diversifying the business strategy by primarily focusing on domestic trade due to the uncertain international trade environment.
- The company continues to explore the possibility of entering into the manufacturing sector to diversify its businesses and mitigate future business risks.
- The company maintains a dedicated in-house Treasury Management desk operating under a Board-approved Hedging Policy to manage currency exposures using structured derivative instruments.
